# Results — Study 704 (Three Drives)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **three
Fibonacci-proportioned drives (each correction retracing 0.382-0.886 of the drive before it, each
drive extending the prior correction by 1.13-2.618x) exhaust a trend and mark a reversal at the
third drive**. A 4% percentage **ZigZag** marks the swing pivots; a candidate is six consecutive
alternating pivots (point 0 through point 5) whose leg ratios land on that Fibonacci grid, with
each drive genuinely extending the one before it. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints in the data stamp below.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC, auto-adjusted (total-return), public, no key |
| Basket | SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM, ^GSPC, ^IXIC, ^DJI, GLD — broad indices/ETFs, deep daily history |
| As-of | **2026-06-30** |
| Fingerprints | SPY `079eeeacb330` · QQQ `ba4a1e34bb16` · DIA `8484eb68cb8e` · IWM `cfbd1e0dca21` · ^GSPC `cec06bce14e7` · ^IXIC `54d65c6aa4cb` · ^DJI `803513feb661` · GLD `44f6ff1685e4` |
| Detector | 4% percentage **ZigZag** pivots; a Three-Drives candidate requires six consecutive alternating pivots (point 0..point 5) whose two correction legs retrace 0.382-0.886 of the drive before them, whose two drive legs extend the prior correction by 1.13-2.618x, and whose drives 2 and 3 each genuinely extend beyond the one before (the "extending drives" rule) |
| Entry / execution | enter the close **one bar after** point 5's ZigZag confirmation (no look-ahead), fading (trading against) the three drives; 5 bps one-way cost x 2 legs for the net numbers |
| No survivorship | broad-index/ETF *price* tapes, not a cross-sectional single-name panel — no surviving-names selection on the Signal axis |

## The headline — does fading the third drive beat a coin flip?

Pooled across the basket: **3,543** ZigZag pivots (same swing detector as sibling
697-wolfe-waves) → **110** candidate Three-Drives patterns that pass the Fibonacci geometry.

| ticker | pivots | candidates |
|---|--:|--:|
| SPY | 337 | 16 |
| QQQ | 431 | 20 |
| DIA | 275 | 4 |
| IWM | 381 | 10 |
| ^GSPC | 975 | 37 |
| ^IXIC | 612 | 14 |
| ^DJI | 315 | 7 |
| GLD | 217 | 2 |
| **pooled** | **3,543** | **110** |

Fade trade at the headline 20-day horizon (enter next close after point 5, opposite the three
drives):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| gross | **+45.0 bps/trade** (win 50.9%, Wilson 95% [41.7%, 60.1%]) |
| one-sample *t* (gross) | **+0.62** (HAC *t* = +0.62) |
| net of 5 bps costs | +35.0 bps/trade (*t* = +0.48) |
| **coin-flip placebo** (random time + random direction, 1,000 draws) | observed **+45.0 bps** vs placebo mean **-0.2 bps** (sd 53.4 bps) |
| placebo *p* | **0.207** |

**Fading the third drive does not beat a coin flip.** The one-sample *t* sits nowhere near the
desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, and a random bet with the same timing freedom and a fair-coin direction does
about as well.

## Fibonacci-grid placebo — is the specific geometry load-bearing?

Swap the 0.382-0.886 / 1.13-2.618 targets for a random ratio grid, keeping the entire ZigZag
machinery and the "extending drives" ordering rule — the same idiom sibling
468-gartley-harmonic uses for its XABCD grid.

| test | observed fade return (H=20, gross) | placebo *p* | valid draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pooled basket, random-ratio grid | +45.0 bps | **0.262** | 496 / 500 |

The real Fibonacci grid beats roughly 74% of random grids on this one point estimate — but the
placebo does **not** clear conventional significance (*p* = 0.262, well above 0.05), so we
cannot certify that the specific 0.382/0.886/1.13/2.618 numbers carry real information. Combined
with a headline *t* of 0.62, there simply isn't an effect for the ratios to be "load-bearing" for.

## Time-symmetry myth-check — does "symmetric" predict anything?

The pattern's own word is *symmetric*. Every detection is scored by the coefficient of variation
of its three drive-leg bar-counts (lower = more evenly spaced in time); the fade returns of the
more- vs less-symmetric half are compared.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | 110 (median CV = 0.396) |
| more time-symmetric half | **+145.5 bps** |
| less time-symmetric half | **−55.4 bps** |
| Welch *t* (sym − asym) | **+1.39** |

A directionally interesting split — the more evenly-spaced patterns do look better on paper —
but it does **not** clear the *t* ≥ 2 bar either. Reported honestly as a suggestive, uncertified
lean, not a finding: with only 110 detections split in half (~55 each), this is exactly the kind
of post-hoc split that needs a much bigger sample or a pre-registered design before it means
anything.

| threshold | candidates | mean (bps, gross, H=20) | win-rate | one-sample *t* |

| 5% | 97 | +128.2 | 57.7% | +1.66 |
| 8% | 34 | +62.2 | 55.9% | +0.52 |

The 5% setting comes closest (*t* = 1.66) but still doesn't clear the bar, and there's no
monotonic trend across thresholds — the kind of noisy bounce you'd expect from a null, not a
signal that a slightly different knob would have caught.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A deterministic panel builds the Three-Drives geometry from **exact anchor points** (ratios
exactly 0.618 / 1.27, not accumulated per-bar noise, which would fragment a leg into spurious
extra ZigZag pivots) with a tunable planted reversal after point 5.

| world | *n* | mean (bps) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | ~24–50/seed | — | mean **−0.84** (sd 0.80), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** | |
| planted edge = +0.30 (H=20) | 27 | **+1,401** | **+6.87** | **+7.19** |

The null centers modestly below zero — a small, disclosed selection effect shared with sibling
697-wolfe-waves: entry requires a ZigZag-confirmed point 5, i.e. price has already moved against
the drives by the confirmation threshold *before* entry. Every one of 20 null seeds stays inside
±2. A real planted reversal, in contrast, is unmistakable at every horizon:

| horizon | *n* | mean (bps) | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 27 | +535  | +6.09 | +6.11 |
| 10-day | 27 | +1,089 | +6.14 | +6.20 |
| 20-day | 27 | +1,401 | +6.87 | +7.19 |
| 40-day | 27 | +1,666 | +6.61 | +7.01 |

The detector can clearly find a reversal **when one is actually there** — so the flat real-tape
result is a true negative, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Across 110 algorithmically-detected Three-Drives patterns (SPY + a 7-ticker
  basket, 1993→2026), fading the third drive nets **+45.0 bps** at *t* = **+0.62** — far short of
  *t* ≥ 2 — and sits inside a coin-flip placebo cloud (*p* = **0.207**). Flat at every
  horizon (5/10/20/40 days, |*t*| < 2 throughout) and across every ZigZag threshold (3%-8%, no
  monotonic trend). A synthetic control proves the harness *would* detect a real planted
  reversal (*t* up to 6.9), so this is a genuine null, not a broken test.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no edge to charge costs against, and the sample is thin
  (110 detections across 8 tapes over 20-30+ years — a handful a year).
- **"Are the Fibonacci ratios load-bearing?" — BUSTED.** The ratio-grid placebo does not clear
  significance (*p* = 0.262); the pattern's own word "symmetric" fares no better — the more
  time-symmetric half of detections shows a directionally positive but uncertified lean (Welch
  *t* = +1.39, n = 110). Neither the specific ratios nor the time-symmetry claim carries
  certified predictive content.
